title: Tribe Liaison & Status-Wire Protocol: Incident Playbook
author: Leah Park
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines the Tribe Liaison role and the Status-Wire communication protocol used for coordinated incident response across teams (platform, runtime, SRE, customer success, and engineering tribes). It is intended for incidents with cross-team impact (multi-service degradation, multi-region latency spikes, or model-quality regressions affecting production).

Purpose:
- Reduce cross-team friction and duplicated messaging during incidents.
- Provide a repeatable activation workflow for public and customer-facing communications.
- Offer templates and checklists for rapid, consistent status updates and post-incident evidence collection.

When to activate the Status-Wire:
1) Any P0 or P1 incident declared by SRE / Incident Commander.
2) Sustained SLO deviation > 5 minutes affecting > 1 customer or > 10% of traffic.
3) Model-quality regression that causes repeated error responses or hallucination rates above threshold.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): overall incident authority; owns triage decisions and escalation to execs.
- Tribe Liaison (TL): single named engineer from each affected tribe. TLs consolidate technical findings and represent their team on the Status Wire. Responsible for:
  - Rapidly validating impact and proposed mitigations for their domain.
  - Contributing one-line status and next steps for each wire update.
  - Collecting evidence artifacts (logs, traces, perf snapshots).
- Bridge Operator: manages the incident bridge, recording timeline and action items.
- Communications Lead (Comms): drafts customer-facing updates, coordinates legal/compliance review if required.
- Customer Success Rep: prepares prioritized customer impact list and coordinates direct outreach where needed.

Activation checklist (first 10 minutes):
1. IC declares incident and sets severity.
2. Pager alert: On-call SRE acknowledges and opens bridge.
3. IC assigns an engineered TL per affected tribe (platform, runtime, model-infra, console).
4. Bridge Operator posts Status-Wire channel link (Slack #status-wire-<incident-id>) and pins initial incident summary.
5. TLs post immediate 1-line: "{team}: impact (yes/no), likely root area, immediate mitigation". Example: "Runtime: partial KV-cache eviction causing 40% increased tail latency; restarting cache nodes as mitigation"
6. Comms drafts and posts first customer notice (see templates).

Escalation matrix (quick reference):
| Role | Primary | Secondary | Escalation threshold | Contact method |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Incident Commander | SRE Lead on-call | Eng Director on-call | >30 minutes to containment | Pager / Phone |
| Tribe Liaison | Team on-call engineer | Team tech lead | No mitigation found in 20 minutes | Slack DM / Pager |
| Comms Lead | Support Ops | Head of CS | Customer SLA breach or regulatory impact | Slack / Email |

Runbook snippets (copy into service runbooks):
- inference-gateway:
  1) Check service health: curl -fsS https://health.redwood.internal/inference-gateway/metrics || true
  2) Query recent traces: otel-cli query --service inference-gateway --last 15m
  3) If error-rate > 2% and tail-latency > 800ms, toggle canary fallback: curl -XPOST https://admin.redwood.internal/route/fallback -d '{"route":"/generate","model":"gptx-small-fallback"}'
- kv-cache:
  1) Inspect eviction log: gcloud logging read "resource.labels.instance_id=\"kv-cache\"" --limit 200
  2) Rehydrate hot-keys from snapshot: /opt/tools/kv-rehydrate --snapshot s3://redwood-cache/snaps/latest --keys hot-keys.txt

Status-Wire messaging cadence:
- Initial (T+10m): Brief impact, services affected, immediate mitigations in progress, expected next update in 30 minutes.
- T+30m: Progress update including measurable signposts (error-rate, latency, traffic diverted) and next steps.
- Every 30—60m afterward: update until containment. Shorten cadence to 15 minutes if customer-impacting or high uncertainty.
- Containment achieved: merge into final incident summary and begin postmortem timeline.

Customer-facing templates (copy/paste-ready):
- Short status page entry (public):
  Title: "Degraded API latency for text generation — investigating"
  Body: "We are investigating increased latency affecting text-generation API requests in US-West. Impact: intermittent delays up to ~4s for a subset of requests. Current actions: rolling restart of KV cache nodes and routing a portion of traffic to fallback model variants. Next update: in 30 minutes. Affected customers will receive direct notices if they meet SLA thresholds."

- Email / CS message (for affected customers):
  Subject: "Service update: transient delays for Redwood text generation — {incident-id}"
  Body: "Hi {customer_name},

We are actively responding to an incident affecting text-generation latency in {region}. Some requests are experiencing elevated latency or transient errors. Our SRE and runtime teams have deployed mitigations (cache restarts and traffic routing) and are monitoring recovery. We will provide another update at {time} or sooner if status changes. We apologize for the disruption and will share a detailed post-incident report within 72 hours.

If you require escalation or mitigation assistance (e.g., pinning model variants or temporary throttling), reply to this message and your Customer Success lead will coordinate.

— Redwood Support"

Game day and simulation plan (quarterly):
- Objective: exercise cross-tribe coordination and Status-Wire to validate SLAs and communications.
- Frequency: quarterly for SRE + product-critical tribes; monthly light drills for new joiners.
- Duration: 90 minutes.
- Roles assigned in advance: IC, Bridge Operator, 3 TLs, Comms, CS.
- Scenario example: synthetic KV eviction at scale causing 30% tail latency increase and 5% error-rate.
- Success criteria: containment within 45 minutes, customer-facing update within 10 minutes, complete evidence capture (traces/logs/metrics) uploaded to incident ticket.

Post-incident evidence & postmortem template:
- Attachments required in postmortem: timeline (with T+ minute markers), logs (last 60 minutes per service), relevant traces (span IDs), Mitigation steps, Root cause analysis, Action items with owners and SLA for completion.
- Postmortem outline (use this header structure):
  *Summary*
  *Impact* (customers, SLOs)
  *Timeline* (bullet list with timestamps)
  *Root Cause*
  *Contributing factors*
  *Immediate remediation*
  *Long-term fixes*
  *Action items (owner + due date)*
  *Verification plan*

On-call rotation fairness & handoff checklist:
- Primary rotation length: 9 days (3-person rotation recommended for fairness).
- Shadowing: new on-call engineers shadow for 2 rotations.
- Handoff checklist (mandatory before shift end):
  1) Confirm no ongoing incidents assigned.
  2) Share any active mitigations, experiments, or rollouts in last 12 hours.
  3) Verify Escalation list and on-call contacts are up-to-date.
  4) If any open action items: add clear owner and ETA.

Bridge & tooling references:
- Incident bridge template: Zoom link pinned in channel; Google Doc timeline template: https://docs.internal.redwood/incident-timeline-template
- Dashboards:
  - SRE Living Dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/ll1/sre-living-dashboard
  - Model Quality Monitor: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/mq/model-quality
  - Token-level cost/latency: Console -> Observability -> Token Insights
- Runbook registry: Confluence runbook index (add link to service runbook pages).

Quick checklist for the Tribe Liaison (TL):
1) Join bridge and post one-line status.
2) Verify logs and traces for your domain and attach evidence to bridge notes.
3) Propose emergency mitigation and estimate time-to-contain.
4) Commit to follow-up artifact (e.g., heap dump, timeline snippet).

Appendix: sample Slack status-wire message (copy-paste)
```
[Status-Wire] Incident: INF-2026-842
IC: @sre-oncall
Services: inference-gateway (P), kv-cache (P)
Runtime: Restarting 2/3 cache replicas; expected partial recovery in ~12m. Error-rate peaked at 4.1%; tail latency 95p=950ms. Next update in 30m.
TLs: @runtime-tl (runtime), @platform-tl (platform), @modelinfra-tl (model)
```

Operational notes & governance:
- All incident owners must file a postmortem for P0/P1 incidents within 72 hours of containment.
- Action items must be tracked in the central incident board and have clear owners and due dates.
- Quarterly reviews: the Incident Review Council will audit a sample of postmortems for completeness and follow-through.
